solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seal line of light bites well on the turn

indicators.note: something on the turn is facing the other way, so the word for well is read back to front
whatever bites takes something between its jaws, so one piece holds the other inside it

blocks.note: a ray is a narrow beam of light
fit means healthy, in good shape

explanation.surface: A sealed-off ray of light seems to cut into a well as it swings round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like the noun, a water shaft, but it is the adjective meaning healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify a treaty is to formally approve it, the same act as setting a seal on it.

clue.text: Quiet picking up a bill that’s unopened

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking up means lifting, so the word for 'a' reads upwards, backwards
something unopened has not had its front opened, so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: 'a' as in 'ten pounds a head' means per, for each
a bird's bill is its beak, and a beak is slang for a nose

explanation.surface: Someone quietly collects an unopened bill from the doormat.
explanation.walkthrough: The trap is reading 'a bill' as an invoice. 'a' is PER, reversed to REP, and the bill is the beak or NOSE, minus its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is a noun for rest, stillness and calm, which is what quiet means here.

clue.text: Not about to wrap present up immediately

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word not is spelt backwards
wrapping goes all the way round something, so one piece encloses the others

blocks.note: taken as written
a person who is present is here
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to gift-wrap a present straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed word is split in two so that it can wrap round both of the following pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereupon is a formal adverb meaning directly after that, at once, without delay.

clue.text: Fried food waste

blocks.note: first meaning: a piece of fruit, vegetable or meat dipped in batter and deep-fried
second meaning: to squander, as in to throw away time or money bit by bit

explanation.surface: A complaint that fried food is a waste.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a remark on leftover chip-shop scraps, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a battered deep-fried morsel; the verb, usually with 'away', means using up money or time pointlessly.

clue.text: Ways to escape and duck headless alien

indicators.note: without a head means the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: outs are ways out of a difficult situation
the eider is a sea duck, famous for its down

explanation.surface: An alien flees its pursuers and a headless duck is left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like a verb to go with 'escape', but it is a noun naming the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider is someone who does not belong to a group, a stranger or foreigner to it.

clue.text: One Parisian cool and outstanding

blocks.note: un is French for one
cool and collected both mean calm and composed

explanation.surface: A Parisian is praised as both calm and remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise, but it means still owed or unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstanding debt or parcel is one still waiting to be gathered in, not yet paid or picked up.

clue.text: Time to split plants on felt tile

indicators.note: splitting a word breaks it apart, so another letter goes in the gap

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
sets are young plants or bulbs ready for planting, like onion sets
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gardeners are told when to split their plants on a felt roofing tile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' is old slang for a hat, so a felt tile is a felt hat, not roofing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is the broad-brimmed cowboy hat, traditionally made of felt.

clue.text: Bee right over swallows

indicators.note: a word that swallows something takes it inside itself

blocks.note: when a thing is over it is done, finished
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A bee flies right over something and gulps it down.
explanation.walkthrough: DONE swallows R to give D-R-ONE. 'over' looks like a position word but is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is the male honeybee, which does no work and exists to mate with the queen.

clue.text: Surplus rails due to be recycled

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and made into something new, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Leftover railway track is due for recycling.
explanation.definitionFit: Residual means remaining or left over, like a surplus that has not been used up.

clue.text: Bird having ooze around it

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word for ooze runs backwards

blocks.note: a wound weeps when it oozes fluid
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird is found with slime all over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like it wraps the ooze round 'it', but here it only turns the first piece back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit is another name for the lapwing, a wading bird named for its cry.

clue.text: Ranks of English whisked round Loch Ness endlessly

indicators.note: with no end, the name loses its final letter
whisking stirs things up thoroughly, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ranks of English tourists are rushed round Loch Ness.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish place names look like scenery, but they are simply the letters to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Echelons are levels or grades within an organisation, such as the upper ranks of the army.

clue.text: Dubious spasm on muscles rotating case of alcohol

indicators.note: something rotating spins round to face the other way, so the word for muscles is reversed
in an across entry, one piece on another follows it
a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: pecs are the chest muscles, short for pectorals
a tic is an involuntary muscle twitch
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A doubtful case of muscle spasm brought on by too much drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of alcohol' suggests a crate of bottles; it means only the outside letters of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sceptical describes someone doubtful or unconvinced, inclined to question claims.

clue.text: Vessels around Portugal not good sign

blocks.note: ca is short for circa, Latin for around or approximately
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
ill means bad, as in ill will
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Ships sailing around Portugal are seen as a bad omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships, but these are blood vessels. 'around' is not a container here but CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Capillaries are the tiniest blood vessels, linking arteries and veins throughout the body.

clue.text: While away, stay apart from American

indicators.note: apart from means excluding, so those letters are taken out of the word

blocks.note: to stay a sentence or an execution is to suspend it
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to hang around while they are away, unless you are American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'While away' is a phrasal verb, not 'during an absence'. 'stay' in the legal sense is a postponement.
explanation.definitionFit: To while away an afternoon is to pass the time, which is to spend it.

clue.text: Effects from entering a pub in April near Barking area

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so these letters go wild into a new order
a piece entering goes inside another one

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written
PH is the map abbreviation for public house
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Belongings are recovered after a visit to a pub one April, near Barking.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is also a district of east London, which hides the anagram signal. A PH goes inside the shuffled letters, then A for area ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Effects are personal belongings, and paraphernalia means miscellaneous gear and possessions.

clue.text: Rogue has to be deleted from Early English novel with lecherous style

indicators.note: rogue means out of order or out of control, so the three letters may come in any order
deleted from means removed out of the longer phrase
novel means new, so the leftover letters make a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, letters removed in any order
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scoundrel is cut out of an early English novel for being too lewd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like a character in the novel but is a shuffle signal for HAS. Take H, A, S out of EARLY ENGLISH and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone with lustful intent, so acting leeringly is behaving in a lecherous manner.

clue.text: One exciting city uncovered in range overlooking hill

indicators.note: removing the covers takes off the outside, leaving only the inner letters
one piece goes in another
in a down entry, a piece overlooking another sits above it

blocks.note: an Aga is a brand of cast-iron kitchen range, a British cooker
the inner letters with the first and last removed
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone excitable is found in a city in the mountains, high above a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' suggests mountains, but it is the kitchen kind; an Aga is a cast-iron cooker common in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator is a person who stirs people up, rousing them to protest or unrest.

clue.text: Officer’s cycle stand from the 1920s

blocks.note: a general is a senior army officer; the apostrophe S comes along
a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: An officer's bicycle stand, dating from the 1920s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand' looks like a rack for parking a bike, but it means a stand taken in protest. The General Strike was Britain's nine-day national stoppage in 1926.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a collective stand against employers, and the famous British one happened in May 1926.

clue.text: Run sale without a fuss

indicators.note: without means lacking, so one letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an auction is a sale by bidding
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone urges you to run a sale without making a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruction is a noisy disturbance or row, a big fuss.

clue.text: Admit colour blue is pronounced

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the words are judged by their sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: to ink is to colour in, and blue means smutty or lewd

explanation.surface: Someone confesses their pronounced colour blindness, or a vivid blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' is not a colour here but means rude, like a blue joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone to a club or group is to let them in, to include them.

clue.text: Mostly going nowhere is dull

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a dead end is a road, or a job, going nowhere

explanation.surface: A complaint that a stalled career is mostly boring.
explanation.definitionFit: To deaden a sound or pain is to make it less sharp, which is the verb sense of dull.

clue.text: Subject of toy piece oddly missing

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered letters missing, only the second and fourth ones are kept

blocks.note: a spinning top is a classic toy
the even-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: A toy has a strange piece missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like 'strangely' but means drop the first, third and fifth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject of a discussion, essay or conversation, the theme being talked about.

clue.text: Dressing to cover concerning cut

indicators.note: covering something goes all round it, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a pad of gauze is a wound dressing
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a dressing to cover a worrying cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like the wound, but it is the definition in its past-tense verb sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Pared means trimmed or sliced away thinly, as with nails or apple peel.

clue.text: Irresistible vice, dad troubled with it

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed or stirred up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the first letters to be rearranged
taken as written and added to the mix

explanation.surface: A father is troubled by a vice he cannot resist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something addictive is so habit-forming that it is very hard to refuse or give up.

clue.text: Stop ass going into Italian city

indicators.note: a piece going into another is placed inside it

blocks.note: Turin is the city in north-west Italy
a nit is a fool, an idiot

explanation.surface: Someone shouts at a donkey trotting into an Italian city to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ass' suggests a donkey, but it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Turn it in is a British idiom telling someone to quit or pack something up.

clue.text: Handled bore

blocks.note: first meaning: having lugs, the ear-shaped handles on a jug or pot
second meaning: carried something heavy, the past tense of bear

explanation.walkthrough: 'Handled' looks like a verb, but it is an adjective meaning fitted with handles; 'bore' is the past tense of bear, not a tedious person.
explanation.definitionFit: A lug is a projecting handle, and to lug is to haul a heavy load with effort.

clue.text: Disrespect of sport opponents involved in dives

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it

blocks.note: RU is short for rugby union
a dive or a den is a seedy drinking place
East and South are opponents at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Sporting rivals show disrespect by diving in the penalty area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dives' looks like football play-acting, but it means shady bars; bridge players sit North, East, South and West, so East and South are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudeness is impolite behaviour that shows a lack of regard for others.

clue.text: Know some cycled from Africa

indicators.note: cycled means moved round in a loop, so a letter moves from the back to the front

blocks.note: ken is Scottish for know
any as in 'have you any bread', meaning some

explanation.surface: Someone knows a few cyclists who came from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Kenya is famous for its distance runners, which makes 'cycled' look like a sport. ANY with its Y brought to the front gives YAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kenyan is a native of Kenya, a country in East Africa.
